sources: arXiv 2408.11142 (ISLES 2024 dataset paper); journal version: Radiology: Artificial Intelligence, DOI 10.1148/ryai.250603
arXiv 2505.18424 ('How We Won the ISLES'24 Challenge by Preprocessing') — fetched 2026-09-01
In-house payload verification: archive member manifest and probe-023 census, evidence/decisions.md entries 2026-08-25 and 2026-08-26 (archive md5 36ae28b9..., Zenodo record 16813698)
verified_dataset_facts.modalities_per_case: Acute session (ses-01): non-contrast CT, CT angiography, 4D CT perfusion, and derived perfusion maps (Tmax, CBF, CBV, MTT) in NCCT space; plus large-vessel-occlusion masks and Circle of Willis anatomy masks. Follow-up session (ses-02): post-treatment MRI (DWI and ADC) and a binary infarct mask derived from the follow-up MRI, registered to NCCT space (filename token space-ncct, payload-verified).
verified_dataset_facts.ground_truth: Binary final-infarct masks delineated on 2-9 day post-treatment (post successful reperfusion) MRI (DWI/ADC), distributed registered to acute NCCT space. Annotator count and algorithm-assistance details not verified from the abstract; flagged in unverified_claims where load-bearing.
verified_dataset_facts.cohort_and_split: 245 patients total: 149 public training cases (payload-verified: 149 cbf maps, 149 rawdata NCCT; 150 lesion-mask rows with one duplicate; sub-stroke0043 ses-01 CBF is a source-corrupt archive member), 96 hidden test cases. Multi-center, hyperacute CT <24h from onset, all cases thrombectomy-treated with follow-up after successful reperfusion per the data paper summary.
verified_dataset_facts.license_access: CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 on Zenodo record 16813698 (train.7z, 99.0 GB; clinical_data-description.xlsx). Public download, no gatekeeping.
verified_dataset_facts.official_evaluation: Dice coefficient, Absolute Volume Difference (AVD), lesion-wise F1, Absolute Lesion Count Difference (ALCD) — quoted from arXiv 2505.18424.
verified_dataset_facts.clinical_data: Demographics, patient history, admission NIHSS, 3-month mRS (Zenodo description). In-house payload check confirms phenotype ses-02 outcome.csv exists (decisions.md 2026-08-28). Onset-to-imaging times and TICI/reperfusion grades not yet verified as released variables.
verified_dataset_facts.winning_method_facts: The ISLES'24 winning method is a large 3D residual-encoder nnU-Net trained with 'only CT inputs, specifically non-contrast CT (NCCT) scans for the submission'; custom CT windowing was the decisive preprocessing step; mean hidden-test Dice 28.5 (SD 21.27) (arXiv 2505.18424). Two consequences used below: (a) the winner never consumes the perfusion maps; (b) the benchmark's absolute performance ceiling is strikingly low.

all_questions.question: Is the NCCT-only winning model using net water uptake — the tissue's water clock — to overrule the CTP core map exactly where that map is known to lie (the ghost infarct core)?
flags: radiologist_word_X: net water uptake / ghost infarct core

all_questions.question: Is every model using the acute hypoperfusion footprint as a hard outer bound, so that ground-truth infarct outside it — embolization to new territory, procedural infarcts — is a structural floor on benchmark error?
Is the model using depth beneath the brain surface — collateral reachability, the internal borderzone — to write off deep voxels at the same perfusion values where it spares cortical ones?
Is the model using the direction the contrast front arrives from — surface-inward retrograde filling versus center-outward antegrade filling — as its collateral pressure gauge?
Is the model using the geometric roughness of the hypoperfusion boundary — interface stability in the growing-front physics sense — as its infarct-growth gauge?
Is the model using a luxury-perfusion rim around the deficit as the signature of a clot that has already opened?
all_questions.drop_reason: Ill-posed keystone: luxury perfusion is predominantly a post-recanalization phenomenon and this cohort is imaged pre-thrombectomy, so the natural experiment may have near-zero support; unsure the question is answerable in this dataset.

all_questions.question: Is the model using the venous sinuses' brightness — the patient's hematocrit — to recalibrate every perfusion number in the head?
all_questions.drop_reason: Sounds obviously wrong (reading a blood count off a head CT) yet is not immediately refutable (blood HU tracks hemoglobin linearly and hematocrit biases CTP quantification); dropped because it is the same venous-HU measurement family as killed idea-028 (IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE) with no new identification strategy.

all_questions.question: Is the model using the hyperdense clot's length and density — the clot burden — to forecast whether reperfusion will succeed?
all_questions.drop_reason: Duplicates backlog candidates isles24-scout-003-c02 (clot occupancy) and isles24-scout-002-c05 (clot permeability); nothing new to add over entries already awaiting development.

all_questions.question: Is the model using old lacunes and white-matter scars as a map of this brain's private hemodynamic history?
all_questions.drop_reason: Dies like killed idea-044 (the old stroke inside the new forecast, IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE) and overlaps backlog isles24-scout-001-c04 (frail brain); no changed fact.

all_questions.question: Is the model using ventricular asymmetry — the first millimeters of mass effect — as an early severity gauge?
all_questions.drop_reason: Entangled with killed idea-035 (fixed-volume pressure vessel) and idea-030 (edema-displaced ground truth), and at <24h the expected effect sits near the measurement floor — the idea-043 EFFECT_UNREACHABLE lesson.

The generic 'no more than two candidates on any single dataset' quota is superseded by the isles24 charter, which mandates that every candidate concretely use ISLES'24; all five are on ISLES'24 by charter design. Zero revivals: nothing in the portfolio brief has externally changed — the unblock conditions for ideas 021, 022, 025, 039, 040, 041, 042 all await either operator decisions or assets that have not appeared, and the 023-arc artifacts (per_patient table, bin_tissue_audit, mirror_qc) already feed active ideas 045/046 through their own lineage. candidates.entry_point_basis: Documented gap: CTP threshold cores systematically overestimate final infarct in early-imaged, successfully reperfused patients — the 'ghost infarct core' (Boned et al. 2017, JNIS; Ballout et al. 2023 systematic review, J Neuroimaging DOI 10.1111/jon.13127). The ISLES'24 cohort is exactly this population (hyperacute CT, follow-up after successful reperfusion), and the challenge exists because learned models beat threshold maps at final-infarct prediction.
candidates.title: The ghost core and the water clock: what the NCCT-only winner knows that the perfusion thresholds don't
candidates.question: Is the NCCT-only winning model using net water uptake — the depth of early ischemic hypodensity — to overrule the CTP threshold core exactly where the ghost-infarct-core literature says that core is a lie?
candidates.rung: Target rung 2 (the model's overruling of the threshold core is organized by measured NWU at matched perfusion). Moves to rung 3 only via a successor HU-edit counterfactual (synthetically deepening/shallowing hypodensity at fixed anatomy), which is deliberately deferred — counterfactual-synthesis is the portfolio's most overused template.
candidates.deliverable_sentence: The model is using net water uptake — how much water the ischemic tissue has already absorbed, read as hypodensity depth on the plain CT — to decide how much of the CBF<30% 'core' will actually survive.
candidates.X_measurement: Net water uptake, NWU = (1 - D_ischemic/D_contralateral) x 100, computed from NCCT HU averaged over the deficit region versus a region-level contralateral reference (Broocks et al., Stroke 2018, DOI 10.1161/STROKEAHA.118.020507, PMID 29976584; Minnerup et al., Ann Neurol 2016 for onset-time calibration). Region definition machinery (Tmax>6s, erosion, per-patient p98 vessel exclusion) already exists in-house from probe 023. Computable on an unseen scan today, by script, with no human annotator: yes.
candidates.suspected_signal: Ischemic edema accrues water quasi-monotonically over the first hours; hypodensity depth therefore encodes (time-since-onset x injury severity). A low-CBF region with almost no water uptake is young tissue that successful reperfusion can still save — the ghost core; the same CBF with deep hypodensity is committed. An NCCT-only model that predicts final infarct at all must be reading some such NCCT quantity; NWU is the physiologically named, radiologist-legible candidate.
candidates.design_template_justification: Two final-infarct estimators with disjoint inputs — the reproduced NCCT-only winner (never sees perfusion) versus the standard CTP threshold core (never sees NCCT) — and the object of study is where and why they disagree. This is the template's genuine meaning, used only twice before in the portfolio.
candidates.use_vs_association: Within-patient conditioning: at matched (CBF value, Tmax value, tissue class), does the probability that the model spares a threshold-core voxel rise as regional NWU falls? Matched-perfusion organization of the disagreement field by NWU is the rung-2 claim; bare correlation of NWU with outcome across patients is explicitly not the readout.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Acute NCCT, derived perfusion maps, and the follow-up-derived lesion mask coexist per case on a common NCCT-space grid, so voxelwise conditioning across NCCT and CTP-derived quantities is possible.
candidates.keystone_evidence: Archive member manifest quoted in evidence/decisions.md (2026-08-25): 'train/derivatives/sub-stroke0001/ses-01/perfusion-maps/sub-stroke0001_ses-01_space-ncct_cbf.nii.gz (+cbv, mtt, tmax)', 'train/derivatives/sub-stroke0001/ses-02/sub-stroke0001_ses-02_space-ncct_lesion-msk.nii.gz', 'train/raw_data/sub-stroke0001/ses-01/sub-stroke0001_ses-01_ncct.nii.gz'; counts 149 cbf / 149 NCCT. Probe-023 takes 12-13 empirically processed NCCT together with the maps on the common grid (label-blind map pass completed 100/100, including the per-bin NCCT HU tissue audit).
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: (1) The published winner recipe (arXiv 2505.18424: residual-encoder nnU-Net + custom windowing) is reproducible well enough that our local model is a faithful stand-in for 'the winning model' — attribution will be scoped to 'an NCCT-only model of the winning family' until proven closer. (2) A region-level contralateral HU reference is adequate despite imperfect head symmetry; in-house mirror_qc.csv (99 cases) supports region-level adequacy (median registration error 1.41 voxels — fatal for voxel mirroring, tolerable for regional means). (3) NWU noise does not swamp the conditional signal.
candidates.rung_reached: Rung 2 if the smallest experiment succeeds; rung 1 (mere sensitivity) if only unconditioned association survives.
candidates.dies_like_prior: No killed idea matches. Nearest neighbor is backlog isles24-scout-002-c01 (the edema clock, SCOUT_ONLY, never developed): that card asks whether a model can read onset time; this one asks whether the verified NCCT-only winner's disagreement with the CTP threshold core is organized by water uptake — a different object (cross-estimator disagreement field), anchored to two newly verified facts (NCCT-only winner; ghost-core cohort match). Against the dominant IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE pattern (x12): the design never compares across patients unconditioned; all primary contrasts are within-patient at matched perfusion values.
candidates.closest_prior_work: Boned et al. 2017 (JNIS, ghost infarct core) and Ballout et al. 2023 (J Neuroimaging, DOI 10.1111/jon.13127) document threshold-core overestimation but never ask what a learned model does about it. Broocks et al. (Stroke 2018, DOI 10.1161/STROKEAHA.118.020507) established NWU as edema biomarker; Minnerup et al. 2016 used it for onset timing. The winner paper (arXiv 2505.18424) shows NCCT-only wins but offers no account of what NCCT signal substitutes for perfusion. Delta: nobody has tested whether a trained final-infarct model's core-overruling tracks NWU.
candidates.existing_assets: Dataset staged and integrity-proven in-house (origin_direct staging, md5-verified, decisions.md 2026-08-26); deficit-region machinery (Tmax>6s masks, erosion, p98 vessel exclusion) from probe 023; per-bin NCCT HU audit code (bin_tissue_audit) already reads NCCT HU inside perfusion strata; mirror_qc.csv registration-error distributions; published winner recipe with exact architecture and windowing; nnU-Net public framework.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Train one fold of the winner-recipe NCCT-only nnU-Net on the 149 training cases (~1-2 GPU-days). On held-out fold cases: compute the CBF<30% (within Tmax>6s) threshold core, the model's predicted mask, regional NWU, and the conditional sparing curve P(model spares voxel | voxel in threshold core; CBF, Tmax, tissue class binned) as a function of regional NWU tercile. Decision: does sparing probability fall monotonically with NWU at matched perfusion, with patient-cluster bootstrap CIs excluding flatness? No ground-truth label enters this primary readout. Secondary (labels): among disagreement voxels, does the model beat the threshold map more often in low-NWU regions?
candidates.standing_confounds_addressed: Scanner/vendor/protocol/site: cancelled in the within-patient matched-perfusion contrast; the across-patient NWU-tercile comparison is exposed to site mix and will be reported with site as a stratum if site metadata exists (unverified). Positioning/habitus: region-level mirror reference tolerates it (mirror_qc evidence). Prevalence/referral: cohort is all-LVO, all-thrombectomy — scope is stated as such. Label leakage: primary readout uses no labels. Not ruled out: NWU is also a severity measure, so 'water clock' is claimed as the physical quantity used, not as proof the model represents time itself.
candidates.alternative_explanations: (1) The model may spare thin-hypodensity core because it reads some other NCCT quantity correlated with NWU (e.g., hyperdense-vessel proximity, sulcal preservation) — partially addressed by also conditioning the disagreement field on distance-to-vessel and testing whether NWU retains conditional organization; fully excluding it needs the successor HU-edit study. (2) Chronic white-matter hypodensity (leukoaraiosis) mimics low-attenuation ischemia — addressed by tissue-class conditioning and excluding periventricular caps. (3) The threshold core itself is computed from maps whose vendor chain is uniform here (icobrain), so 'disagreement' partly measures that one pipeline's idiosyncrasies — scope-limited claim.
candidates.anticipated_negative: Sensitivity-limited: a flat conditional curve says this model does not detectably use water uptake at the achievable NWU precision — still publishable next to the winner paper (the winner's signal is then NOT the obvious physiological candidate), but not decisive against small effects.
candidates.remaining_legwork: Winner-recipe reproduction (2-4 days engineering + 1-2 GPU-days/fold), NWU module (2-3 days, mostly existing code), conditional-analysis harness (3-4 days). First decision in ~2 weeks with a single GPU.
candidates.annotation_burden: None. All quantities are computed by script from released data; no new expert labeling.

clarity.why: One-sentence question with a named quantity and named comparator; loses a point because 'the winning model' is operationally 'our reproduction of the winning recipe'.

identifiability.why: Matched-perfusion within-patient conditioning rules out the main patient-level alternatives, but correlated NCCT signals (vessel sign, sulci) can only be partially excluded without the deferred counterfactual arm.

medical_relevance.why: Ghost core is a live clinical decision problem (whether to treat hyperacute patients with large threshold cores); showing a deployable model has internalized the correction — or has not — changes how its outputs should be read.

interest.why: The NCCT-only winner is a standing puzzle the community has noticed; naming its signal in a radiologist's word is exactly the charter's audience test.

prior_legwork.why: Dataset staged and integrity-proven in-house; deficit and HU-audit machinery exists; winner recipe published; NWU formula published.

feasibility.why: Keystone INSPECTED_TRUE; one nnU-Net fold plus scripted measurements; ~2 weeks to first decision on one GPU.

data_readiness.why: Public Zenodo under CC-BY-NC-SA; 99 GB staging pipeline already proven; one known source-corrupt member (sub-stroke0043) handled by standing exclusion policy.

evaluation_readiness.why: Primary readout is a custom conditional curve (needs pre-registration of bins and margins); official challenge metrics apply only to the secondary arm.

negative_result_value.why: Sensitivity-limited null, but bounded and informative next to the winner result.

novelty_confidence.why: Limited search found no test of NWU-organization of model-vs-threshold disagreement; capped at 3 pending the novelty audit.

regret.why: If another group explains the NCCT-only winner first, the program will regret having had every asset staged and not asking.

Minnerup et al. 2016 Ann Neurol citation details (from memory; formula source Broocks 2018 is verified)
That the winner reproduction reaches leaderboard-comparable Dice (attribution scoped until checked)
candidates.plain_pitch: When a stroke patient reaches the scanner very early, the standard perfusion software often paints a large 'dead core' that turns out to be alive after treatment — clinicians call this the ghost core. Curiously, the model that won the ISLES'24 stroke challenge ignored the perfusion maps entirely and used only the plain CT picture. We ask whether that model is reading the tissue's water content — brain tissue soaks up water hour by hour as it dies, which shows as darkening on plain CT — and using it to overrule the perfusion software's exaggerated core. If true, the model has quietly learned the correction clinicians make by experience, and we can point at it in an image quantity radiologists already know by name.

candidates.entry_point_basis: Well-performing (relative to the field) models with a startlingly low absolute ceiling: winning hidden-test Dice 28.5 (arXiv 2505.18424). Measurement that would detect the unexpected signal: ground-truth infarct mass in components disconnected from and distant to any baseline hypoperfusion, versus predicted mass in the same regions. Artifact it would be confused with: session-to-session registration error and contiguous edema growth displacing the lesion boundary — both act at the boundary and cannot create disconnected components in a different arterial territory.
candidates.title: The unpredictable infarct: how much of the benchmark happened after the scan
candidates.question: Is the model using the acute hypoperfusion footprint as a hard outer bound on its prediction, while a measurable fraction of the ground-truth infarct — new-territory emboli and procedural infarcts — lies structurally outside any model's reach?
candidates.rung: Rung 2 as stated (the support bound is directly observable in model behavior; the out-of-support GT fraction is a census, not an inference). Rung 3 is not the target: no mechanism attribution beyond support geometry is claimed.
candidates.deliverable_sentence: The model is using the acute hypoperfusion footprint as an outer bound on where infarct can be, and the X% of ground-truth lesion volume that lies in separate, distant arterial territory — infarcts that happened after the baseline scan — sets a floor on every leaderboard error metric.
candidates.X_measurement: Per case: (a) baseline deficit footprint = Tmax>6s mask union CBF<30% mask (existing in-house machinery); (b) connected components of the ground-truth lesion mask; (c) per component, Euclidean distance to the footprint (scipy distance transform) and arterial territory label from the deformably registered Digital 3D Brain MRI Arterial Territories Atlas (Liu et al., Scientific Data 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41597-022-01923-0, PMID 36739282; github.com/Chin-Fu-Liu/Arterial_Atlas); (d) 'out-of-support' GT volume = components >20 mm from the footprint or in a non-overlapping territory; (e) the same measure applied to model-predicted masks. Computable today by script: yes.
candidates.suspected_signal: Thrombectomy carries a documented complication: clot fragments embolize to previously unaffected territories, and wire manipulation causes new infarcts; these appear on 2-9 day DWI and enter the ground truth, but no baseline image contains their cause. A model trained on baseline imaging learns that infarct essentially never appears outside hypoperfused tissue and suppresses such predictions.
candidates.design_template_justification: One prior portfolio use. The grammar here is an audit of ground-truth geometry against baseline physiological support — not boundary-drift measurement (the prior use's flavor) and not any intervention. No listed template fits: labels are the object of study, not the truth standard.
candidates.use_vs_association: The use-vs-association trap does not arise in its usual form: the claim quantifies what the model cannot be using (post-scan events leave no baseline trace). The model-side clause ('uses the footprint as an outer bound') is established behaviorally: predicted mass outside the footprint ~ 0 across cases while GT mass outside is > 0 — a per-case observable, not a fitted association.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Ground-truth lesion masks and the perfusion maps coexist per case on the common NCCT grid so that footprint distances are meaningful, and the lesion masks genuinely contain disconnected distant components in some cases (if no out-of-support lesion exists, the census returns zero and the finding inverts).
candidates.keystone_evidence: Common grid: archive manifest quoted in evidence/decisions.md 2026-08-25 ('..._ses-02_space-ncct_lesion-msk.nii.gz' alongside '..._space-ncct_cbf.nii.gz (+cbv, mtt, tmax)'), and probe-023 processed maps and NCCT together on that grid across 99-100 cases. The existence of nonzero out-of-support components is the part NOT yet inspected — deliberately: it is the study's primary count, and its zero outcome is itself decisive (see anticipated_negative). The inspected keystone is the geometry substrate; the census quantity is the deliverable, not the prerequisite.
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: That organizer-side registration of ses-02 masks into NCCT space is not so poor that whole components land in wrong territories — a failure mode that would masquerade as out-of-support lesion. Mitigation is built into the measure (20 mm + territory-disjointness is far above mirror_qc-scale registration error, median 1.41 voxels), and any case with out-of-support mass gets individual visual QC of the registered pair — inspection of specific flagged cases, not new annotation.
candidates.dies_like_prior: Nearest kills: idea-030 (ground truth drawn on a swollen brain) and idea-034 (edge of the map), both IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE. Both died because boundary-level GT displacement could not be separated from true growth. This candidate is restricted by construction to disconnected components at >20 mm in disjoint arterial territories — displacement and contiguous edema act at the boundary and cannot manufacture those. What it shares with 030/034 is only the subject (GT quality); the estimand is component topology, not boundary position.
candidates.closest_prior_work: Embolization to new territory is a documented thrombectomy complication with rates around 5-9% in trial cohorts (memory estimate; flagged unverified). The ISLES'24 papers describe the GT pipeline but do not report how much final lesion lies outside baseline hypoperfusion. ISLES'22 analyses discussed multifocal lesions but on MRI-only baselines. Delta: no published census of baseline-unsupported GT volume for ISLES'24, and no measurement of trained-model behavior against it.
candidates.existing_assets: All 023-arc staging and census machinery; Tmax>6s and CBF-threshold masks already computed for 99 cases in prior takes; lesion masks payload-verified; territory atlas public with deformable registration tooling (ANTs); model-side arm can reuse the c01 nnU-Net fold.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Pure geometry pass over the 149 training cases (no model, no training): compute per-case out-of-support GT volume and component census; report the distribution, the affected-case fraction, and the implied per-metric floor (Dice/AVD/lesion-F1/ALCD are all computable as if a model predicted the supported subset perfectly). One week. Model-side confirmation (predicted masks from one nnU-Net fold: out-of-support predicted mass ~ 0) adds days if c01's fold exists.
candidates.standing_confounds_addressed: Scanner/vendor/protocol/site: irrelevant to the geometry census (per-case, within-case). Registration: addressed by distance + territory disjointness + per-flagged-case visual QC. Label leakage: none — labels are the object. Prevalence/referral: the census is cohort-specific (all-LVO thrombectomy); stated as scope. Not ruled out: whether out-of-support lesions are procedural versus spontaneous new emboli versus missed baseline hypoperfusion below Tmax threshold — the census stratifies components by sub-threshold Tmax (e.g., 4-6s) occupancy to separate 'below-threshold support' from 'no support', but cause attribution beyond that is not claimed.
candidates.alternative_explanations: (1) Registration failure (addressed above). (2) The footprint definition is too narrow — mild hypoperfusion below Tmax>6s supported the lesion after all; addressed by reporting support at multiple Tmax thresholds down to 2s, making 'no support' a graded, checkable statement. (3) Hemorrhagic transformation regions inside the GT mask: these lie within the treated territory and do not create distant components. (4) Duplicate lesion-mask row (payload-known): resolved case-by-case per the standing exclusion policy.
candidates.anticipated_negative: Decisive in both directions: a near-zero out-of-support fraction certifies the benchmark as baseline-supported (a citable validity result for ISLES'24); a substantial fraction quantifies an irreducible error floor and reframes the low leaderboard Dice.
candidates.remaining_legwork: Atlas registration pipeline (2-3 days), component census script (2-3 days), threshold-graded support analysis (2 days), flagged-case QC (1-2 days). First decision in ~1 week of work.
candidates.annotation_burden: None. Visual QC of flagged registered pairs is inspection, not labeling.

clarity.why: The question, measure, and both possible answers are stated in one breath; every term is operationalized.

identifiability.why: Component-topology restriction rules out the boundary-displacement alternative that killed 030/034; residual cause-attribution ambiguity is explicitly out of scope.

medical_relevance.why: Tells clinicians and challenge organizers how much of 'prediction error' is unpredictability — directly reframes how ISLES'24 scores, including the 28.5 winning Dice, should be read.

interest.why: A benchmark-integrity number every ISLES'24 participant would want; the anomalously low leaderboard ceiling makes it timely.

prior_legwork.why: Masks and maps staged and verified; threshold machinery exists; atlas public; model arm optional and reusable.

feasibility.why: Keystone INSPECTED_TRUE; the primary result requires no model training at all — scripted geometry over already-staged data; first result in days.

data_readiness.why: Public data, proven staging; one corrupt member and one duplicate mask row already governed by standing policy.

evaluation_readiness.why: The implied floors are computed in the challenge's own four official metrics; no custom margins needed for the census itself.

negative_result_value.why: A zero result is a publishable validity certification of the benchmark, not a dead end.

novelty_confidence.why: No such census found for ISLES'24 in limited search; capped pending audit.

regret.why: Obvious in hindsight; cheap; the kind of finding another group could publish first from the same public data.

unverified_claims: ENT/procedural infarct rates (~5-9%) in thrombectomy cohorts — memory estimate pending citation

That ISLES'24 GT masks were not manually pruned of new-territory lesions by the organizers (the data paper's GT-pipeline details are unread; if organizers excluded them, the census measures that editorial choice instead — still a finding, but a different sentence)
Atlas deformable registration quality on stroke-deformed brains (mitigated by the distance criterion)
candidates.plain_pitch: During the clot-removal procedure that these stroke patients all received, small clot fragments sometimes drift into fresh brain territory and cause new strokes that only show up on the follow-up scan. The challenge's 'correct answer' masks are drawn on that follow-up scan, so they can contain damage that no baseline image could possibly predict. We will measure exactly how much of the benchmark's correct answer lies outside any tissue that was short of blood at scan time, and confirm that models never predict anything there. Whichever way it comes out, it is a number the whole challenge community needs: either the benchmark is certified fair, or part of every model's 'error' is actually the future, and the surprisingly low winning scores get a partial explanation.

candidates.entry_point_basis: Well-performing final-infarct models with no account of their per-voxel triage rule. Measurement that would detect the unexpected signal: depth-stratified predicted-fate curves at matched perfusion values within patients. Artifact it would be confused with: gray/white tissue-class composition and partial-volume effects, which co-vary with depth — handled by tissue-class conditioning and surface/ventricle-margin erosion.
candidates.title: Written off by depth: the internal borderzone in the model's triage
candidates.question: At matched perfusion values, is the model using depth beneath the pial surface — where leptomeningeal collaterals cannot reach — to predict death for deep voxels while sparing superficial ones?
candidates.rung: Target rung 2 (depth organizes predicted fate at matched perfusion and tissue class, within patients). Rung 3 would need input edits that vary apparent depth at fixed perfusion — geometrically contrived; honestly out of reach, and stated as such.
candidates.deliverable_sentence: The model is using distance from the brain's surface — a proxy for how reachable tissue is by surface collateral vessels — to write off deep white matter and basal ganglia at perfusion values where it predicts cortical survival.
candidates.X_measurement: Per-voxel Euclidean distance from the brain-mask surface (scipy/SimpleITK distance transform on the NCCT brain mask), plus tissue class (gray/deep-gray/white) from the registered arterial/anatomical atlas (Liu et al. 2023 atlas hierarchy includes lenticulostriate territory) or HU-based classing. Computable today on an unseen scan by script: yes.
candidates.suspected_signal: Leptomeningeal collaterals perfuse the cortex from the surface inward; deep white matter and lenticulostriate territory are end-arterial with no collateral back-door — the radiologist's 'internal borderzone'. At identical Tmax/CBF snapshots, deep tissue has objectively worse rescue prospects, and a well-trained model should have discovered this. The question is whether it did — which is mechanism discovery, not confound elimination: either answer tells physicians what the model's triage rule is.
candidates.design_template_justification: Shares the conditional-observational grammar with c05; justification for both surviving: c03 is a voxel-level within-patient contrast of model output against a static geometric coordinate, c05 is a patient-level shape statistic predicting growth — different unit of analysis, different X family, different failure mode probed (triage rule vs growth gauge).
candidates.use_vs_association: Within-patient matched-perfusion contrast: fate difference between depth strata at the same (CBF, Tmax, tissue class) cells, patient-cluster bootstrapped. Patient-level covariates (site, severity, protocol) cancel; 'the model uses depth' is claimed only as conditional organization of its own outputs, rung 2, with the limitation stated that a perfusion-matched depth-varying input edit (rung 3) is not credibly constructible.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Perfusion maps and NCCT on a common grid with enough deep-and-superficial co-occurrence of matched perfusion values within single patients — i.e., the (CBF, Tmax, tissue, depth) cells needed for the contrast are actually populated in real deficits.
candidates.keystone_evidence: Common grid and map existence: archive manifest quotes in evidence/decisions.md 2026-08-25 (as c01). Cell occupancy is supported by probe-023's completed stratification machinery: take-13 census analyzed 99/100 cases with per-patient CBF percentile bands within the eroded Tmax>6s deficit meeting frozen coverage floors (decisions.md 2026-08-30) — demonstrating that within-deficit, within-patient perfusion strata are populated at usable size. Depth co-occupancy within those strata is the residual (below).
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: That matched-perfusion cells span the depth axis within patients often enough (deficits confined to one depth stratum contribute nothing). This is checkable label-blind in a half-day occupancy audit before any model work, and that audit is the first gate of the smallest experiment.
candidates.rung_reached: Rung 2 if the conditional contrast is populated and non-flat; rung 1 otherwise.
candidates.dies_like_prior: Nearest kill: idea-038 ('does the model price the last mile of blood delivery?', IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE). The family resemblance is real — both concern delivery geometry. The difference: 038-class designs compared across patients where delivery geometry co-varies with occlusion site, protocol, and population; here every contrast is within-patient at matched perfusion and tissue class, and depth is a per-voxel geometric coordinate computed identically for every case, not a per-patient anatomical classification. Also adjacent: idea-032 (spare route, killed) classified anatomy variants — nothing here classifies anatomy.
candidates.closest_prior_work: Clinical literature establishes differential vulnerability and the internal borderzone concept (textbook physiology; deep perforator territories infarct at lesser insults). ML literature on final-infarct prediction (e.g., Nielsen et al. 2018, Stroke, deep learning vs thresholds — identifier from memory, unverified) does not decompose model triage by geometric depth. Delta: no published depth-stratified behavioral audit of any stroke final-infarct model.
candidates.existing_assets: 023-arc staging + within-deficit stratification code (percentile bands, erosion, vessel exclusion) directly reusable; c01's trained fold reusable as the model under test (full-modality variant trainable identically); atlas public.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Gate 0 (half-day, label-blind, no model): occupancy audit of (CBF-band x Tmax-band x tissue x depth-stratum) cells across 149 cases. If populated: run one trained fold (reuse/extend c01), compute within-patient predicted-fate differences between deep and superficial members of each matched cell, aggregate with patient-cluster bootstrap. First decision ~1 week after c01's fold exists. Secondary (labels): does ground-truth fate show the same depth organization — i.e., is the model's rule physiologically right?
candidates.standing_confounds_addressed: Scanner/vendor/protocol/site/habitus/prevalence: cancelled within patient. Tissue composition: conditioned explicitly. Partial volume at surface and ventricle margins: eroded margins on both ends of the depth axis. Label leakage: primary readout is model behavior, label-free. Not ruled out: depth-dependent perfusion-map reliability (deconvolution SNR may vary with depth) — audited by comparing map noise statistics across depth strata before interpreting; and depth correlates with distance-to-occlusion, which is a genuine physiological cousin (both are 'delivery cost') — the claim names depth-as-collateral-reachability but cannot fully separate it from arterial path length; stated openly.
candidates.alternative_explanations: (1) Depth-dependent map artifacts (audited, above). (2) Atlas/tissue misclassification in deformed brains (HU-based fallback classing; erosion). (3) The model may key on basal-ganglia-specific appearance rather than depth per se — testable by comparing deep white matter vs deep gray at matched depth: if the effect is structure-specific rather than depth-graded, the sentence changes and says so. (4) Training-set label statistics (deep tissue more often infarcted in GT) could teach the rule without the model 'reading' geometry from this image — this is what 'using depth' means behaviorally; the claim is about the rule, not its training origin.
candidates.anticipated_negative: Sensitivity-limited: flat depth curves at matched perfusion bound the model's depth use below the occupancy-limited detectable size; informative but not decisive against small effects.
candidates.remaining_legwork: Occupancy audit (half-day); depth/tissue module (2-3 days); model fold (shared with c01); analysis harness (3-4 days). First decision ~1-2 weeks given c01 proceeds; ~3 weeks standalone.

clarity.why: Precise conditional question; 'depth as collateral reachability' vs 'arterial path length' ambiguity honestly costs a point.

identifiability.why: Within-patient matched-cell design excludes patient-level factors; depth-correlated map reliability and path-length cousinhood remain named residuals.

medical_relevance.why: If models triage by depth, clinicians should know it (it matches physiology but changes how per-voxel outputs are trusted in deep vs cortical tissue); if not, a physiologically expected rule is missing — actionable either way.

interest.why: Solid mechanism-discovery question; less surprising than c01/c02 because the physiological prior is strong.

prior_legwork.why: Stratification machinery from 023 is nearly the whole pipeline; model shared with c01.

feasibility.why: Keystone INSPECTED_TRUE; gate-0 occupancy audit costs half a day and kills cheaply if cells are empty.

data_readiness.why: Same staged public data as siblings.

evaluation_readiness.why: Custom conditional readout requiring pre-registered bins; no external benchmark applies.

negative_result_value.why: Sensitivity-limited but occupancy-bounded — the audit states in advance what effect size was detectable.

novelty_confidence.why: No depth-stratified model audit found; limited search.

regret.why: Worth having but less time-critical than c01/c02.

unverified_claims: Within-patient depth-spanning occupancy of matched perfusion cells (gate 0 checks this before any model work)
candidates.plain_pitch: The brain's surface can borrow blood from neighboring arteries through a network of surface back-roads, but tissue deep inside the brain has a single supply line and no back-up. Radiologists know this, and deep tissue really does die more easily during a stroke. We ask whether the challenge-winning kind of stroke-outcome model has taught itself this rule: when two brain regions look equally starved of blood on the scan, does the model give up on the deep one and hold out hope for the one near the surface? Either answer helps a physician: it reveals the model's triage rule in terms of an anatomical concept they already use.

candidates.entry_point_basis: Well-performing perfusion-consuming models. Measurement that would detect the unexpected signal: the filling-direction index — alignment between the Tmax spatial gradient and the depth gradient inside the deficit. Artifact it would be confused with: deconvolution and AIF-delay artifacts imposing spatial structure on Tmax, and quantized Tmax values making gradients blocky — both named, both auditable label-blind.
candidates.title: The blood arrives backwards: filling direction as the model's collateral gauge
candidates.question: Is the model using the direction the contrast front travels through the deficit — surface-inward retrograde filling versus center-outward antegrade filling — as its gauge of collateral pressure when it decides how much penumbra survives?
candidates.rung: Target rung 2 (model salvage predictions organized by filling direction at matched deficit size/severity). The named successor for rung 3 is a synthetic arrival-order reversal (counterfactual family, deferred by portfolio-homogenization discipline).
candidates.deliverable_sentence: The model is using the direction of bolus arrival written in the Tmax map — delay increasing from the brain's surface inward, the image of retrograde collateral filling — as its collateral pressure gauge when it forecasts how much of the threatened tissue will survive.
candidates.X_measurement: Filling-direction index (FDI): within the eroded Tmax>6s deficit (vessel voxels excluded via the in-house p98-CBV rule), compute the smoothed spatial gradient of Tmax and the gradient of depth-from-surface; FDI = mean cosine alignment of the two fields. Positive FDI = delay grows inward (surface fills first: retrograde pattern); negative = delay grows outward (antegrade residual trickle through/around the clot). Construct anchored to multiphase-CTA collateral assessment, where retrograde pial filling defines collateral status (Menon et al., Radiology 2015, DOI 10.1148/radiol.15142256; Menon 0-5 collateral score). Computable today on an unseen scan by script: yes.
candidates.suspected_signal: A specific physical quantity: the propagation direction of the contrast arrival front, determined by which vascular route delivers blood to the occluded territory — antegrade (through/past the clot) versus retrograde (backwards through surface collateral networks). Radiologists read exactly this pattern from multiphase CTA to grade collaterals; the Tmax field is a denser encoding of the same arrival-time physics, and a model consuming Tmax has the direction available at every voxel.
candidates.design_template_justification: The X is not a scalar covariate but the geometric alignment of two vector fields, and the readout includes a spatial-structure prediction (the model's predicted-growth zone should sit at the far end of the filling direction — last-fed tissue dies first). No listed template captures a field-direction audit; conditional-observational is the nearest but loses the directional-prediction content.
candidates.use_vs_association: Within-patient, same-acquisition signed index; association with model-predicted salvage at matched deficit volume and severity is rung 1-2; the spatial arm sharpens it — X must predict WHERE the model places growth (directional structure), not merely how much, which generic severity correlates cannot mimic. Rung-3 use requires the deferred arrival-order-reversal counterfactual.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: The released Tmax maps carry usable spatial gradient structure inside deficits — sufficient value resolution and smoothness that a per-voxel gradient direction is signal, not quantization noise.
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: Map existence and grid are payload-verified (manifest, decisions.md 2026-08-25), but Tmax value quantization (often 0.5s steps in vendor maps) and icobrain smoothing behavior have not been inspected; if Tmax is coarsely quantized, gradients are blocky and the FDI needs heavier smoothing or fails. This is the honest Mode C keystone, checkable label-blind in one afternoon on already-staged cases.
candidates.rung_reached: Rung 1-2 if measurable; the afternoon quantization audit is the first gate.
candidates.dies_like_prior: Nearest kill: idea-032 (the arterial network's spare route, IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE) — collateral anatomy classification across patients. Difference: no anatomy is classified; FDI is a within-patient signed field statistic computed from one acquisition by one formula for every case. Nearest live siblings: backlog isles24-scout-001-c01 (collateral clock — scalar timing volumes) and idea-042 (delay vs dispersion — temporal curve shape); this candidate is about spatial direction of the arrival field, which neither touches.
candidates.closest_prior_work: Menon et al. 2015 (Radiology, DOI 10.1148/radiol.15142256) established retrograde pial filling as the readable collateral signature on multiphase CTA; automated multiphase-CTA collateral scoring exists (deep-learning graders). Perfusion-gradient literature exists for Tmax-based severity but as scalar summaries. Delta: no work computes an intra-deficit arrival-direction field and asks whether a trained final-infarct model's spatial predictions are organized by it.
candidates.existing_assets: Staged dataset; deficit/erosion/vessel-exclusion machinery (023); depth-field code shared with c03; full-modality nnU-Net trainable with the same recipe infrastructure as c01.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Gate 0 (one afternoon, label-blind): Tmax quantization and gradient-coherence audit on staged cases — distribution of distinct Tmax values, gradient magnitude vs smoothing scale, FDI stability under resampling. If measurable: compute FDI for 149 cases, train/reuse one full-modality fold, test (a) FDI vs model-predicted salvage fraction at matched deficit volume (patient-cluster bootstrap), and (b) the directional arm: alignment between the model's predicted-growth centroid displacement and the local filling direction. First decision ~2-3 weeks.
candidates.standing_confounds_addressed: Scanner/vendor/protocol/site: within-patient index; the across-patient FDI-vs-salvage comparison is exposed to site/protocol mix and is reported stratified where metadata allows. Positioning: depth field is patient-intrinsic. Label leakage: primary readouts are model-behavior, label-free. Not ruled out: AIF selection and deconvolution implementation impose spatial delay structure of their own — partially auditable (uniform icobrain chain; contralateral hemisphere provides a null field where no collateral physics applies: FDI computed in the mirrored healthy region should be ~0, an internal negative control), but not fully excludable at rung 2.
candidates.alternative_explanations: (1) Deconvolution/AIF artifacts (contralateral null-field control, above). (2) Venous contamination at the surface pulling Tmax down superficially — vessel exclusion plus sensitivity analysis excluding the outermost cortical ribbon. (3) FDI may proxy deficit depth-composition (deep deficits fill differently) — condition on deficit centroid depth and tissue mix. (4) The model may use collateral-correlated intensity features (e.g., CTA vessel conspicuity) rather than the arrival direction itself — rung-2 wording claims the gauge, not the unique channel; stated openly.
candidates.anticipated_negative: Sensitivity-limited: quantization bounds the detectable directional signal; the gate-0 audit converts this into a stated sensitivity floor before any model work, so a null is bounded rather than empty.

cross_domain.borrowed_construct: Front propagation in porous/branching media (hydrodynamics): the arrival-time field of an invading fluid encodes the geometry of its supply routes; flow direction is normal to arrival-time isochrones.
cross_domain.implied_measurement: Treat Tmax as an arrival-time field and read supply direction from its gradient — the FDI.
cross_domain.if_analogy_dropped: FDI degrades to a descriptive Tmax asymmetry statistic: still computable, still testable against model behavior, but the collateral-pressure interpretation and the sign prediction (surface-inward = retrograde = better-protected penumbra) lose their physical warrant.

candidates.remaining_legwork: Gate-0 audit (one afternoon on staged data); FDI module (2-3 days); full-modality fold (1-2 GPU-days); directional analysis (1 week). First decision ~2-3 weeks.

mechanism_clarity.why: A specific physical quantity (arrival-front direction) with a defined measurement (Tmax-gradient/depth-gradient alignment) and a radiologist-recognized referent (retrograde pial filling); short of 5 because isolating it from deconvolution-imposed structure is designed but not proven.

identifiability.why: Within-patient signed index, contralateral null-field control, and a directional spatial prediction that severity scalars cannot mimic; deconvolution artifacts remain the live alternative at rung 2.

interest.why: 'The model can see which way the blood is coming in' is a genuinely new, physician-legible reading of a perfusion map; connects CTP models to the multiphase-CTA collateral literature.

medical_relevance.why: Collateral status drives treatment decisions; a model shown to read filling direction earns (or forfeits) trust on collateral grounds clinicians can interrogate.

clarity.why: One-sentence question with a signed, defined index; the retrograde/antegrade dichotomy simplifies a continuum.

feasibility.why: Informational (Mode C, outside priority): capped at 3 by NOT_INSPECTED keystone; the afternoon audit resolves it cheaply either way.

novelty_confidence.why: Informational (Mode C, outside priority): limited search found no intra-deficit arrival-direction model audit.

negative_result_value.why: Informational: sensitivity-limited but pre-bounded by the gate-0 audit.

prior_legwork.why: Informational: deficit machinery exists; FDI and directional analysis are new code.

evaluation_readiness.why: Informational: fully custom readout; margins must be invented and pre-registered.

candidates.priority_note: Mode C weighting per rubric: 0.30 mechanism_clarity + 0.25 identifiability + 0.20 interest + 0.15 medical_relevance + 0.10 clarity = 3.75. Feasibility and novelty_confidence reported outside the score per Mode C rules.
unverified_claims: Tmax value quantization/smoothness in the released icobrain maps (the keystone; gate-0 audit)
That 'last-fed tissue dies first' is the correct directional prior for the spatial arm (physiological plausibility argued, not sourced)
Automated multiphase-CTA collateral-scoring literature details (seen in search results, not read)
candidates.plain_pitch: When a clot blocks a brain artery, blood can sometimes sneak in backwards through detour vessels that run over the brain's surface — and on a timing map of the scan, you can see which direction the blood actually arrived from, because tissue fed by detours fills surface-first, in reverse. Radiologists already grade these detours by eye from a related scan type and use the grade to guide treatment. We ask whether a stroke-outcome model, given the timing map, is reading that direction of arrival — effectively judging the quality of the detour supply — when it decides how much threatened tissue will survive. This is a speculative, mechanism-first idea: the first step is simply to check whether the released maps are sharp enough for the direction to be measurable at all.

candidates.entry_point_basis: Well-performing models predicting growth beyond the core. Measurement that would detect the unexpected signal: multiscale roughness (perimeter-area/surface-volume scaling) of the Tmax>6s isocontour at matched deficit volume, against model-predicted growth. Artifact it would be confused with: map smoothing/resolution and multi-embolic fragmentation inflating apparent roughness — both named and controlled.
candidates.title: The rough edge grows: boundary geometry as the model's stability gauge
candidates.question: Is the model using the geometric roughness of the hypoperfusion boundary — the fingered edge of an unstable supply front — as its gauge of which deficits will grow into their penumbra?
candidates.rung: Target rung 1-2 (honest): roughness-organized model growth predictions at matched deficit volume. Rung 3 would need boundary-reshaping input edits (counterfactual family, deferred).
candidates.deliverable_sentence: The model is using the roughness of the hypoperfusion deficit's boundary — smooth edges meaning pressure-supported equilibrium, fingered edges meaning marginal unstable supply — as a collateral-stability gauge when it forecasts infarct growth.
candidates.X_measurement: Multiscale boundary roughness of the Tmax>6s isocontour: surface-area-to-volume scaling exponent across smoothing scales (box-counting / perimeter-area method), computed per case on the largest connected deficit component after erosion and vessel exclusion; matched-volume analysis so roughness is not a size surrogate. Standard image-analysis code (scikit-image/ITK); no annotator. Computable today on an unseen scan: yes.
candidates.suspected_signal: The deficit boundary is the standing front where collateral perfusion pressure balances the occlusion's deficit. In interface physics, a front supported by ample, evenly distributed driving pressure relaxes smooth; a front at marginal supply develops fingers along local weaknesses (Saffman-Taylor instability as the archetype). A fingered Tmax boundary would be the geometric signature of collateral supply running at its margin — tissue about to lose the standoff — and a growth-predicting model has the geometry available.
candidates.design_template_justification: Second use in this set alongside c03 — justified because the unit of analysis (patient-level shape statistic vs c03's within-patient voxel contrast), the X family (boundary geometry vs geometric coordinate), and the probed failure mode (growth gauge vs triage rule) all differ; the shared grammar is conditioning on matched severity, which any honest observational design here requires.
candidates.use_vs_association: Matched-volume, matched-severity association of roughness with model-predicted growth fraction is rung 1; the analogy supplies a falsifiable sign and locality prediction (growth should occur preferentially at the fingered boundary segments, not uniformly) — a spatial claim generic severity correlation cannot mimic. Rung-3 use requires boundary-reshaping edits, deferred.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Deficit-boundary roughness is measurable above the smoothing/resolution floor of the released Tmax maps — i.e., between-patient roughness variance exceeds what map processing alone imposes.
candidates.keystone_residual_assumption: Maps exist on a common grid (payload-verified, decisions.md 2026-08-25), but icobrain's smoothing kernel and the effective resolution of the Tmax field have not been inspected; if processing dominates boundary shape, roughness measures the pipeline, not the physiology. Honest Mode C keystone; checkable label-blind in ~2 days (roughness distribution vs smoothing-scale curves, plus contralateral-hemisphere pseudo-boundaries as a processing-noise floor).
candidates.rung_reached: Rung 1 if measurable; the measurability audit is the first gate.
candidates.dies_like_prior: Nearest kill: idea-020 (a spreading front inside the perfusion deficit, IDENTIFIABILITY_FAILURE) — it inferred dynamics from a single snapshot. This candidate deliberately claims only static geometry as a gauge (rung 1-2) and ties direction to a named physical instability rather than inferring motion; if the critic finds even the static claim unidentifiable, the kill is cheap (two gates, ~1 week). Also adjacent: isles24-scout-005-c05 (sulci pin the predicted edge, backlog) concerns anatomical pinning of the predicted boundary, not supply-front stability.
candidates.closest_prior_work: Perfusion-lesion shape features appear in radiomics outcome papers as anonymous texture covariates; the interface-stability interpretation and the matched-volume, boundary-local growth test are absent. Saffman-Taylor/kinetic-roughening literature (physics) supplies the construct, not the application. Delta: no work tests whether a final-infarct model's growth forecast is organized by boundary roughness, nor whether growth localizes to rough segments.
candidates.existing_assets: Staged dataset; deficit machinery (023); GT lesion masks for the secondary (does growth actually localize to rough segments — a label-using exploratory arm); model fold shared with c01/c04.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Gate 0 (~2 days, label-blind): roughness measurability audit — per-case multiscale roughness curves, contralateral pseudo-boundary noise floor, variance decomposition. If measurable: matched-volume association of roughness with model-predicted growth fraction (one fold, reusable), plus the locality arm (predicted growth adjacency to rough vs smooth boundary segments within patients). First decision ~2 weeks.
candidates.standing_confounds_addressed: Scanner/vendor/protocol/site: single processing chain (icobrain) is uniform across the cohort — a scope statement, not a control; within-patient locality arm cancels patient-level factors. Fragmentation: analysis restricted to the largest connected component with component count as covariate. Volume-roughness coupling: matched-volume design. Label leakage: primary arms label-free. Not ruled out: occlusion-site anatomy shapes both boundary geometry and growth risk (an MCA-M1 deficit's boundary crosses different tissue than an M2's) — occlusion-site stratification from the released LVO masks (payload: LVO masks exist per Zenodo description) partially addresses; residual anatomy coupling stated.
candidates.alternative_explanations: (1) Roughness proxies deficit anatomy/occlusion site (stratified, above). (2) Processing noise (gate-0 floor). (3) Roughness proxies severity depth (condition on mean Tmax within deficit). (4) The appeal-of-the-sentence check the style rule demands: 'fingered fronts' is a seductive image, and per the style rule this is flagged — the physics analogy is load-bearing for the sign prediction and the candidate is scored with identifiability 2 accordingly.
candidates.anticipated_negative: Sensitivity-limited: a null bounds roughness use below the gate-0-stated floor; if gate 0 itself fails (processing dominates), the candidate dies for the cost of two days and leaves a reusable map-resolution fact for the whole portfolio.

cross_domain.borrowed_construct: Kinetic roughening / viscous-fingering instability of driven interfaces (statistical physics): interface morphology encodes the stability margin of the driving-force balance.
cross_domain.implied_measurement: Multiscale roughness scaling of the deficit isocontour as a stability readout.
cross_domain.if_analogy_dropped: Roughness becomes an uninterpreted shape covariate — the association remains testable but there is no predicted sign, no locality prediction, and no physician-legible sentence; the analogy is what elevates this above radiomics fishing, and the card says so.

candidates.remaining_legwork: Gate-0 audit (2 days); roughness module (2-3 days); model fold shared; locality analysis (1 week). First decision ~2 weeks.

mechanism_clarity.why: A named physical construct (interface stability under marginal driving pressure) with a defined measurement (multiscale roughness scaling) and a sign prediction; short of 5 because the chain from collateral pressure to Tmax-contour morphology has unmodeled steps (tissue heterogeneity also fingers fronts).

identifiability.why: Matched-volume and locality arms help, but boundary geometry is entangled with occlusion-site anatomy and processing, and the candidate's appeal partly rests on its imagery — flagged per the style rule.

interest.why: Imports a falsifiable physics construct into stroke imaging with a concrete locality prediction; surprising if true, cheap to kill if not.

medical_relevance.why: A validated boundary-stability gauge would be a new bedside-readable collateral proxy, but the path from rung-1 association to clinical meaning is longer than for c01-c03.

clarity.why: Precise measure and matched-volume design; 'roughness' admits several estimators, pinned to one before scoring.

feasibility.why: Informational (Mode C, outside priority): capped by NOT_INSPECTED; two-day gate resolves.

novelty_confidence.why: Informational: radiomics adjacency makes novelty genuinely uncertain; audit must search shape-feature outcome literature specifically.

negative_result_value.why: Informational: bounded null plus a reusable map-resolution fact.

prior_legwork.why: Informational: machinery partially exists; roughness estimation is new but standard.

regret.why: Informational: the least regret-prone of the five if skipped.

candidates.priority_note: Mode C weighting per rubric: 0.30x4 + 0.25x2 + 0.20x4 + 0.15x3 + 0.10x4 = 3.35. Feasibility and novelty_confidence reported outside the score per Mode C rules.
unverified_claims: That LVO occlusion-site masks support the planned stratification granularity (Zenodo description confirms masks exist; contents unread)
Absence of a prior radiomics paper testing precisely perimeter-area scaling of Tmax contours against model-predicted growth (novelty risk flagged)
candidates.plain_pitch: When one fluid pushes into another with barely enough pressure, the front between them doesn't stay smooth — it breaks into fingers, a pattern physicists know well from oil and water. During a stroke, detour blood supply holds a front against the spreading shortage, and we suspect a smooth front means the detours are holding comfortably while a fingered, ragged front means they are at their limit. We ask whether stroke-outcome models are reading that raggedness when they forecast which brains get worse — and specifically whether the worsening they predict happens along the ragged stretches of the front. The idea is speculative, and step one is just to check the released maps are sharp enough to measure raggedness at all — if not, we stop after two days.

cycle_self_check.use_vs_association_check: Each card carries a one-line use_vs_association statement; all five lead with X (a physician-legible quantity) rather than confound elimination, per the last-cycle correction.
